## Intent
Hypothesis: a mask intermediate decoupling decide from respawn enables compiler auto-vectorization of the per-particle integration loop, approaching the streaming ceiling.

## Layout & approach
The AoS layout packs 11 fields into 69 B/particle; loop 1 touches 28 of 68 B (41% hot), loop 2 touches 4 of 68 B (5% hot), loop 3 touches 28 of 68 B (41% hot). At 69 B/p each particle spans two cache lines — every access pulls 128 bytes to use 28. The mask approach writes a 1 B/p verdict in loop 1, then scans it in loop 2 to drive respawn. The 68-byte stride should enable across-particle vectorization, but mixed-field AoS confines packed ops to within-particle shuffles. All measured points are L3-resident or DRAM (L2 spill at N≈7598).

## Cache saturation
N=10K/100K are L3-resident, N=1M/10M are DRAM (L3 spill at N≈243K). At q=0.01 the L3→DRAM rise is modest — 25.2 to 27.2 ns/p (8%) — because the 41% hot fraction wastes bandwidth regardless of level. At q=0.1 and q=0.25 the transition steepens to 21–24% (26.1→31.5, 27.8→34.4): respawn's random spawn writes hit cold lines in DRAM. At q=0.5 the rise is only 12% (31.6→35.3) because per-particle respawn overhead dominates. The algo is never cache-saturated — it is frontend-starved.

## Bandwidth
Achieved 2.0–2.8 GB/s against 12.69 GB/s ceiling — 16–22%. Memory floor is 5.437 ns/p; actual is 24.6–35.3 ns/p, 4.5–6.5x the floor. Not bandwidth-bound: frontend_stall dominates at 64–72%, compute 16–36%, backend_stall near zero at q=0.01 rising to 9–11% at q=0.1/0.25 in DRAM. Against baseline: 0.97–1.02x at q=0.01, degrading to 1.14x at q=0.25 in DRAM, recovering to 0.91–1.01x at q=0.5. Against the winner: 1.8–3.3x slower everywhere, worst at q=0.01 (3.3x) where the winner vectorizes.

## Assembly
No across-particle vectorization: vector-suffixed instructions = 0. Loop 1 processes one particle per 68-byte stride (`add rbx, 0x44`), using scalar `vmovss`/`vmulss` for age and `vmovups`/`vmulps`/`vaddps` for pos/vel — packed ops shuffle components within one particle, not across lanes. The mask is a single `mov BYTE PTR [r12+r14*1], al`. Loop 2 scans with `vmovdqu`+`vptest` for 32-byte blocks, then unrolls 32 individual `cmp BYTE PTR`/`je` checks, each conditionally `call`ing spawn — 35 calls, 34 `vzeroupper`. This 619-instruction footprint with 40 `je` branches drives the 64–72% frontend_stall. Loop 3's byte-granular scatter (`movzx`/`cmovae`/`mov BYTE PTR`) adds further pressure.

## Verdict
Refuted — the mask intermediate does not enable auto-vectorization. The compiler emits zero across-particle SIMD: the 68-byte AoS stride confines packed ops to within-particle shuffles, and the 619-instruction branchy respawn scan drives frontend_stall to 64–72%. The algo is 0.97–1.02x baseline at q=0.01 but 3.3x slower than the winner, degrading to 1.14x baseline at q=0.25 in DRAM. At q=0.5 it is 1.8x slower than the winner and merely matches naive scalar (0.91–1.01x). The 41% hot fraction and 2-line-per-particle access cap bandwidth at 16–22% of ceiling.
